summary: Heinrich August Jäschke was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a Moravian Church missionary from 1857 to 1868, later teaching Heinrich Wenzel and Arthur Coke Burnell.

Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer at Leipzig, Karl Benedikt Hase in Paris, and at Calcutta. He held posts at Fort William, Doveton, and Aliah University.

Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1839 to 1843. He held a post at the University of Munich from circa 1865 to 1894 and taught Albert Grünwedel.

Ewald worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Thomas Christian Tychsen, he taught at Große Schule (1822–1824), the University of Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867), and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

Heinrich Hettrich worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Saarland and Giessen, he completed his habilitation at Munich. He taught at Marburg and Würzburg, where he held the chair of comparative linguistics from 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann studied linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Munich under August Schleicher and Martin Haug. He held posts at Leipzig University (1876) and as comparative linguistics professor at Strasbourg (1877).

Heinrich Kiepert was a historian, archaeologist, and geographer. He studied at Frederick William/Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann and at Jena. He held posts at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Léonard de Chézy. He held the chair of oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

Heinrich Lenz studied at the Imperial University of Dorpat from circa 1820 to 1823. He held posts at Saint Peter's School, Saint Petersburg State University, the Main Pedagogical Institute, and the Mikhailovsky Artillery School.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and at Munich. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and the Humboldt University of Berlin, where he was chair from 1909 to 1935.

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1886) and University of Strasbourg (~1886–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).

Heinrich Rückert was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from circa 1852 to 1867 and at the University of Breslau from circa 1867 to 1875.
Heinrich Schliemann was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Paris from 1866 to 1868 and at the University of Rostock circa 1869.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe, and later served as ordinary professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Zurich (1841–1889).
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1863 to 1867. From 1868 to 1911, he served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, later completing his habilitation at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying under Scherer, Goldschmidt, Roth, and Weber. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics (1881), and Berlin's Celtic chair (1901–1910).

Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg. He worked as an assistant at Heidelberg in 1965 and served as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Erich Frauwallner. He served as an assistant at Saarland, Privatdozent at Mainz, and Chair of Indology at Göttingen from 1965 to 2000.

Heinz Mode was an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, under Malalasekera and Fischer, and at Basel. He served as professor of Oriental archaeology at the University of Halle from 1948 to 1978.
